name: vibration-budget
description: Chapter 5: 3 catastrophic overcharge blasts crater nuisance and ecology scores. Finding #9: the file's original premise ("exceed vibration budget 3 times... verify $5,000 fine is applied") has no implementation anywhere in the codebase to test — recordVibration (ScoreManager.ts) only moves nuisance/ecology, no budget counter or cash fine exists, and no event/campaign rule ties one to blast count either. That claim is dropped here in favor of the real, checkable effect (nuisance/ecology cratering); whether a real fine mechanic should exist is a game-design question, out of scope for a test-assertion pass — filed as a follow-up, not silently implemented.

steps.description: #553: switched from `campaign start level:dusty_hollow` -- dusty_hollow's 96x40x96 grid put a manually-bought vehicle's grid-centre spawn far enough from the drill sites to add real travel time on top of an already-long 3-cycle file (campaign start has no staffed:true equivalent, and staffed:true itself doesn't fit here either -- see the drill_plan step below). size:96 keeps this step's original point (a bigger world than the plain new_game default above) without the campaign wrapper. Cash bumped to $250,000, then to $400,000 (#557): 3 catastrophic blasts each need a fresh driller+drill_rig (see below), $36,000 a cycle, on top of payroll/upkeep during 3 separate drilling waits -- #557's own crew-geometry fix (see the living_quarters build step, now after blast 1) hires employee #3 a full cycle earlier than before and stretches the file's own tickCount well past its pre-#557 figure (999 -> 1481, see the final finances step's own note), so payroll/upkeep now runs for materially longer; $250,000 was no longer enough headroom to reach grid 3's own vehicle purchase without a real, traced insufficient-funds stall, and $350,000 (the first bump tried) still finished the file $2,834 short of solvent (direct-traced) -- $400,000 clears grid 3's own purchase with real margin and ends the file solvent.

expect.note: createScoreState's neutral baseline (ScoreManager.ts), before any blast — the 3 that follow must crater ecology/nuisance from here

steps.description: #699: arms forceShiftRestIfNeededByPolicy (#678) -- state.sitePolicy.revision is 0 (unapplied) until this runs. continuous, not shift_8h: SHIFT_DURATIONS_TICKS.shift_8h is 8 ticks, shorter than a single drill_hole action, so applying it this early interrupts the queued vehicle-gated drilling below before it can land a single hole (confirmed live -- drilling stalled at holeCount:0 with shift_8h applied here, the exact trap tutorial-interactive.json's own #681 fix already documents and avoids). continuous has no shift-length cap but still forces rest on hunger/fatigue (shouldForceRest checks that in every mode), which is all this file's own short 4-hole cycles need.

#553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action — a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole — so each of this file's 3 blast cycles now needs its own fresh crew: rumblox at this overcharge is genuinely lethal (Finding #9's honest premise), and the driller/drill_rig that just drilled a site routinely dies/is destroyed in its own blast (sandbox-measured), so a new one is hired for each grid rather than reused. Fired again right after each blast (see below) so a surviving-but-idle driller from an earlier cycle doesn't drag the roster's average wellbeing down across the whole file and risk a worker_revolt on cycle 3.

#553: a fresh driller for grid 2/3 — see grid 1's own hire step for why (a new one each cycle, fired after each blast). #553-followup: no toolbar click here -- the preceding `time resume` step already opened the employees panel (it clicks `#bs-toolbar [data-panel="employees"]` itself, see its own #601-followup note) and the `finances` step between it and this one is a command-only observe step that never touches panel state, so the panel is still open. ToolRail's click handler is a togglePanel toggle (UIManager.ts:450) -- re-clicking here closed the panel outright, leaving the driller row zero-size for the click that followed. #601-followup: `employeeCount` switched from `equals: 1` to `changedBy: 1`, matching this project's own preferred convention for a running total (scenario-defs.md) and grid 3's own hire step (see its note) -- grid 1's driller now dies deterministically in both modes (see the preceding step's own note) and is never spliced in either one any more, so the baseline this hire step starts from is 1 (the corpse, never fired), not 0. `changedBy` proves what this step's own action did without pinning a baseline a future edit upstream would have to keep in sync by hand. Hired alongside the first driller rather than several blast cycles later (#556). Ordering the quarters is real queued work now, so the crew reaches this file’s long drill/charge stretch later and more worn; one driller carrying it alone under the continuous policy this file applies reached well-being zero and held it past REVOLT_TICKS, ending the level in the worker_revolt whose LevelEndScreen this file’s own step-3 note describes covering the Blast panel.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants blasting at Rookie (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), but no role starts with driving.drill_rig -- without it the driller could never staff the drill_rig just bought. The player-facing path is training at a driving_center; skipped here since this file isn't about training.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:2 depth:6 start:10,10 diameter:0.089
steps.description: Grid 1/3. The spacing stepper defaults to 3m (DEFAULT_SPACING_M, Drill.ts); one decrement click on the strip's spacing stepper (data-field="spacing") lowers it to 2 before dragging, so the (10,10)-(12,12) rectangle computes the declared 2x2. #553: spacing tightened from the original 4m to 2m to keep 3 separate drill/blast cycles' total drilling time (a fresh driller/drill_rig each time, see above) reasonable. depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, all 3 grids in this file): none of the 3 drill_plan steps click the depth stepper, so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default. Unlike tutorial-playthrough.json's real divergence, this file's own assertions (decreased/equals:0 on already-floor-clamped nuisance) are directional and floor-based, so they already tolerated the real (more violent, shallower) blast regardless — confirmed by re-running both modes unchanged after the fix. This is a metadata-only correction, not a behavior fix. #557: position deliberately left at (10,10), not relocated -- moving grid 1 to escape its own padded danger zone (computeDangerZone, Zone.ts) was tried first (start:34,10 and start:10,36, both still clear of grid 2 (20,10) / grid 3 (30,10)'s own hole footprints) and rejected empirically, not on arithmetic: direct command-mode probing (createRunner+runCommand, tick-by-tick, scripts/_probe1.ts-style harness) showed x:34 wedges the lone driller/drill_rig solid (`isMoveStuck:true`, holeCount stalled at 0 for the full 600-tick budget) -- pristine terrain past x:30 in this z:10-12 band is a hard reachability cliff (x:30 drills fine solo, x:31 already wedges), and grid 3's own real run only ever reaches x:30-32 because grid 1's and grid 2's blasts have already carved a path there by the time it runs, which a first-drilled grid 1 can't borrow. z:36 drills fine solo (no stuck flag, well inside budget) but breaks grid 3 a different way: grid 1's blast at z:36-38 no longer clears any terrain along the z:10-12 corridor, so grid 3 at (30,10) -- reachable in the original file only because grid 1's and grid 2's blasts jointly carve that corridor open -- stalls at holeCount:0 exactly like the x:34 attempt did, confirmed by direct full-scenario run. The real fix is relocating living_quarters instead (see that step's own note) -- every viable grid 1/2/3 arrangement shares this z:10-12 band, so their own padded boxes (`x:[-5,27]`/`[5,37]`/`[15,47]`, all `z:[-5,27]`) union into one corridor no on-corridor living_quarters position can be safe from during all 3 cycles; only a z escape works, which is living_quarters' own call to make (#556's central-commute tuning covers all three grids, not grid 1's own drill_plan) and grid 1 stays exactly where every other grid's own reachability depends on it having been. Relocating living_quarters is necessary but not sufficient on its own, though: idle-time dispatch (`claimOnePoolCandidate`, EmployeeDispatchSteps.ts) can still route any idle blasting-qualified employee into grid 1's own charge_hole pool work regardless of where they'd otherwise be resting, so employee #2's own survival also needs the targeted `employee dispatch`/`employee cancel` pair a few steps below, not living_quarters' relocation alone -- confirmed empirically: a living_quarters move by itself still lost employee #2 to grid 1's blast in a live run, exactly this way.

expect.note: 2 rows x 2 cols = 4 holes ordered (ghosts), none drilled yet (#553)

steps.description: #699: cycle 1/3's fixed tick-50 chunk drill wait replaced with waitUntil on holeCount -- with living_quarters/continuous policy now protecting this crew (see the steps above), rest interruptions make each cycle's own drilling take a genuinely variable number of ticks (a fixed budget either stalls short, as cycle 2's own 3-chunk/150-tick budget did against the new trajectory, or wastes ticks the crew doesn't need), matching the waitUntil convention `.claude/rules/scenario-defs.md` documents for 'a wait for queued work to land' and the fix already applied to tutorial-interactive.json/tutorial-steps-visual.json for the identical class of divergence (#681/#689).

expect.note: All 4 holes have landed -- none lost, none left ordered forever.

steps.description: Finding #9 (see file description): the original file charged explosive:boomite, whose maxChargeKg is 8 — amount:15 exceeds it, so batchCharge rejected the whole charge with an error, never applied, never thrown (success:false, silent). chargedCount stayed 0 through the entire charge/sequence/blast pipeline in every run of this file's history — no hole was ever actually charged, sequenced, or blasted, so the file never once produced the catastrophic overcharge it claims to test. Fixed by using rumblox instead — the catalog's own "defining trait: high vibration" product (vibrationMod 1.6, maxChargeKg 20, ExplosiveCatalog.ts), which is also the more honest real product for this file's stated intent. Finding #10: Charge All (chargeAll(), Charge.ts) issues `charge hole:* explosive:${this.selectedExplosiveId} amount:${this.amountKg}kg stemming:${this.stemmingM}m` from the panel's OWN selection state — selectedExplosiveId defaults to boomite (DEFAULT_EXPLOSIVE) and only changes when a product card is clicked (data-action="select-explosive", data-explosive="<id>"). A real browser run confirmed this: without clicking the rumblox card first, every one of this file's 3 charge-all clicks silently applied the panel's boomite/5kg/2m defaults instead of the declared rumblox/15kg/1m — producing a normal, non-catastrophic blast (nuisance barely moved, 50→49.975) instead of the intended overcharge. Fixed by clicking the rumblox product card, then driving the amount stepper 5→15kg (10 clicks, 1kg/click) and the stemming stepper 2→1m (5 clicks, 0.2m/click, data-field="amount"/"stemming") before Charge All — the same class of gap as Finding #4/#5, generalized to explosive selection.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

#554-followup (issue #586 CI): idempotent -- a no-op when nothing is pending, resolves one when a timer fired during the charge-drain wait above (up to 3000 ticks at 8x speed is real time long enough for a random event to land). Without this, a fired-and-unresolved event's own .bs-confirm-overlay backdrop blocks the next click -- real CI reported exactly that (the following `employee fire 1` step's own toolbar-open click never landed, leaving employeeCount at 2 instead of 1 by the checkpoint several steps later).

#601-followup: leading `resolveEventIfPending` added, on the original theory that the preceding `event choose 0` step's own resolve and this step's first click were two separate real-time steps with a gap between them, and a timer event landing in that gap left its `.bs-confirm-overlay` backdrop covering the blast panel, failing this step's own `[data-step="3"]` click with "element is covered by div". #707 (correction): that diagnosis was wrong, the same way #699 already found once for this exact symptom on this exact file (see the build-living-quarters step's own note). CI's `.bs-confirm-overlay` was the LevelEndScreen a genuine worker_revolt raises, not a random event's dialog -- direct-traced (command mode): `state.levelEndReason` reads `'worker_revolt'` partway through the wait_until immediately above this step, before this step ever runs, on both the pre- and post-#707 GameLoop.ts. A loop-until-drained `resolveEventIfPending` could never have closed that, and didn't (confirmed: CI kept failing here after this exact fix landed once already, PR #718's own history). The real fix is the living_quarters relocation in the build step above, which keeps `revolt.ticksAtZero` at 0 for the whole file; `resolveEventIfPending` stays here only for its own genuine, narrower purpose -- an actual pending random event (not a level-ending one) landing in the real-time gap between steps.

#557 fix: pure geometry (moving grid 1 itself, or moving living_quarters far enough to sit outside grid 1's own padded danger zone while a working living_quarters still exists nearby) was tried first and empirically rejected -- see the drill_plan step's own note below for the full trace of both attempts and why each one fails a different way. Debris attenuation (Damage.ts's processProjections, #557's own feature) now reaches out to BLAST_DANGER_MARGIN_M (15m) at reduced but often still-lethal energy, so employee #2 -- idle since hire, with nothing of their own to do until grid 2 needs them -- is a real casualty risk from blast 1's rumblox overcharge no matter where they happen to be resting, INCLUDING when idle-time dispatch (claimOnePoolCandidate, EmployeeDispatchSteps.ts) routes them to help charge grid 1's own holes alongside employee #1 (a real, direct-traced behaviour: any blasting-qualified idle employee is eligible for any open charge_hole pool action, not just the grid's own assigned driller). `employee dispatch <id> x: z:` (TaskDispatch.ts, requiredSkill omitted) sends employee #2 specifically -- and only employee #2, not employee #1, who dies here exactly as originally designed (see the drill_plan step's own note and the hire step's own note above on why that's fine) -- to (30,15): x:30 clears grid 1's own padded zone (x:[-5,27]) with real margin (computeDangerZone, Zone.ts; grid 1's holes are (10,10)-(12,12)), confirmed minable/reachable pristine terrain (the same x:30 grid-1-relocation attempt below drills solo in well under budget), and close enough that the walk itself costs employee #2 almost no morale (direct-traced: arrives near-untouched, morale 97-100/100) -- the single biggest lever against the worker_revolt risk a farther escape (or living_quarters itself sitting this close) reliably triggers a few hundred ticks later. No skill: param -- unlike the assign_skill bootstrap steps, this needs no qualification check, just a destination.

#557: pads out employee #2's short walk to (30,15) before firing -- no state-dump field exists to wait on for one specific employee's own position (waitUntil's field/equals only reads the trimmed scenario state, which has no per-employee x/z), so this is a hand-measured tick count rather than the project's own preferred waitUntil-on-a-real-condition pattern; direct-traced (command mode) to comfortably clear grid 1's own zone boundary well before 60 ticks elapse, with room to spare against the 25+-tile drilling-stall commute trap (#681) this file's other notes describe. Split into 3 chunks of 20 with an `event choose 0` after each (not one bare `tick 60`) because a plain `tick N` command -- unlike `waitUntil`'s own loop -- does not auto-resolve a pending event; it simply stops early the instant one fires mid-block (events.ts), and a real run showed exactly that (an Anthem event fired at tick 215, cutting a bare `tick 60` here down to 1 real tick and leaving employee #2 barely off their starting square when blast 1 fired).
#557: drains any event the tick chunk above left pending, same idempotent pattern already used before the sequence steps in this file (see those steps' own notes).

#557: the `employee dispatch 2 x:30 z:15` step above is only ever meant to get employee #2 clear of blast 1 -- it is not real, ongoing work with anywhere useful to finish, and this step's own intent is to clear it before TaskCancellation.ts's interrupted-work-resume path can hand it back to employee #2 once grid 2's real work is available. #928: action id 43 no longer matches -- direct-traced (command mode) against the current engine, the single-gauge fatigue rebalance (hunger/breakNeed removed, morale-penalty ladder rescaled 3x, SITE_POLICY_DEFAULT_THRESHOLD = 60) shifts this employee into a real proactive rest (`general_work` requeued onto their own `taskQueue`, not held as `activeActionId`) by the time this step runs, rather than still actively walking/holding the dispatch the way pre-#928 timing did -- the dispatch's own real current action id (direct-traced: 28) sits queued-behind-rest at that point rather than actively held. Cancelling id 28 there is a real, pre-existing TaskCancellation.ts defect surface, not a #928 regression: `cancelAction`'s `clearHolderWalkFields` unconditionally clears whichever action is the employee's CURRENT `activeActionId`/task-progress fields whenever `action.holderId` matches them, even when the action being cancelled is only queued behind a different, currently-active action (here, the rest) -- it wipes the employee's real in-progress rest bookkeeping instead of the queued dispatch, which cascades into grid 2's drilling genuinely stalling at 3/4 holes. TODO(#939): unrelated to needs/travel/thresholds, and a correct fix needs its own test coverage across every `cancelAction` caller, not a scenario-file workaround -- see #939 for the reproduction and fix. Direct-traced (command mode): leaving this step's target at the stale id 43 (deterministically not-found, given current engine timing) is harmless -- grid 2's drilling reaches 4/4 holes regardless of whether this housekeeping cancel actually fires, so `commandOutcome: refused` documents the now-genuinely-refused, harmless outcome rather than asserting a cancel this file no longer needs.

expect.note: a fired blast clears the plan back to zero; the rumblox overcharge's real, checkable effect — nuisance and ecology both crater from the 50/50 baseline (recordVibration, ScoreManager.ts) — not the fabricated fine (see file description)

steps.description: #601-followup: was `event choose 0` (resolveEventIfPending) then `employee fire 1`. Direct probe (deathCount right after the blast step above, both modes, run 3x each) shows grid 1's driller now dies deterministically in BOTH modes -- the file's old "not always" is stale, same staleness #601 already found and fixed for grid 2's own analogous transition (see that step's own note, several hundred lines below). A dead employee has no row in #bs-employee-panel (`CrewPanel.render` filters to `e.alive`) -- `.bs-detail-toggle` was never going to exist, so the old toggle/dismiss/confirm `clickIfPresent` chain always no-op'd in interaction mode. But `fireEmployee` (Employee.ts) splices by id with no `alive` check, so the OLD command-mode script (a bare `employee fire 1`) still spliced the corpse for real -- a real player has no click for that, since the row doesn't exist to click. That command-vs-interaction action-count asymmetry is what #601 traced for grid 2 (`runCommand`'s action-count gate charges `employee fire` whether it fires a live employee or a corpse, but interaction mode's genuine no-op charges nothing), and it applies here identically. Fixed the same way #601 fixed grid 2: `time resume` is idempotent this deep into an already-resumed run and, as a META_COMMAND, exempt from the action-count gate in both modes, so neither mode's replay of this step nudges the cooldown gate. The one remaining click -- opening the employees panel, so the hire step below still finds it open -- stays, modeling a player checking on their dead crew and finding nobody left to dismiss. #557: employee #2 survives this blast (dispatched clear before it fired, see the steps above) -- confirmed by direct probe, deathCount reads 1 (employee #1 alone) immediately after the blast step.

#557: grid 3's own driller, hired here -- a full cycle earlier than the original file's own step immediately before grid 3 -- so they can build living_quarters (below) while employee #2 goes straight into grid 2's own drill_plan in parallel, instead of employee #2 idling through the whole construction wait themselves (direct-traced: that idle wait alone cost employee #2 real morale, ~97 -> ~31, before grid 2's own cycle even started, and compounded into a worker_revolt by grid 2's own blast). `employeeCount` stays `changedBy: 1` matching this project's own running-total convention (scenario-defs.md).

#557: living_quarters, built here (after blast 1, not before it) so grid 1's own drill/charge cycle runs with nobody resting near a soon-to-fire zone, and at (20,30) rather than the file's old (16,15) so the building itself -- which cannot evacuate -- sits outside every remaining grid's own padded danger zone (grid 2's is x:[5,37] z:[-5,27], grid 3's is x:[15,47] z:[-5,27]; both share z:[-5,27], so only a z escape clears both at once, matching the drill_plan step's own note on why the corridor can't be dodged in x). z:30 clears that shared z:27 boundary with real margin: a bare-minimum z:28 was tried and rejected empirically -- the building's own 3x3 (T1) approach ring dips back to z:27, still inside the zone, so an employee whose own rest-need routes them back to living_quarters (as any employee's eventually does) walks straight back into danger, undoing the whole point. x:20 balances round-trip commute to grid 2 (centre ~21,11) and grid 3 (centre ~31,11) roughly the way the original (16,15) balanced all three grids before #557 widened the danger radius past what any close-in position could survive.

expect.note: Ordering only queues a construction site (#556); employee #3, just hired above, walks over and builds it while employee #2 goes on to grid 2 in parallel below.

steps.description: Left unmarked: hiring already grants blasting at Rookie (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), but no role starts with driving.drill_rig -- without it the driller could never staff the drill_rig just bought. The player-facing path is training at a driving_center; skipped here since this file isn't about training. #557 (fixed): this step used to be a documented, deterministic KNOWN BREAK -- Damage.ts's processProjections attenuates debris out to BLAST_DANGER_MARGIN_M (15m, was an exact 2m HIT_RADIUS only), and employee #2, idle and resting near the file's old living_quarters at (16,15) (~6.4m from grid 1's holes), was reliably killed by blast 1's rumblox overcharge before ever reaching this step, cascading into every step through the file's end failing. Fixed not by repositioning that one employee's rest spot but by the two steps this file now runs before blast 1 fires (see the `employee dispatch 2` step's own note, several steps up) plus moving living_quarters' own construction to after blast 1 (see that step's own note) -- employee #2 survives deterministically now, confirmed by direct probe, and this assign_skill succeeds.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:2 depth:6 start:20,10 diameter:0.089
steps.description: Grid 2/3. #553: spacing tightened from 4m to 2m — see grid 1's own note. #553-followup: added the toolbar blast-panel click as the first action here (Grid 1/3's own drill_plan step above has one; this one never did) -- by this point in the file the active panel is "vehicles" (opened by the `vehicle buy drill_rig` step just above), not "blast", so `#bs-blast-panel [data-step="1"]` was zero-size until the blast panel was actually opened. Also dropped the spacing-decrement click that used to run here: DrillStep.gridSpacing (Drill.ts) is a single instance field, mutated only by the stepper's onDec/onInc and never reset between grid cycles -- Grid 1/3's own decrement already took it from the 3m default down to 2m, and that persists across this whole scenario (BlastPanel/DrillStep is never recreated), so decrementing again here dropped it to 1m (Math.max(1, 2-1)) and turned this rectangle's 2x2 grid into a 3x3 (round(2/1)+1 = 3 per side, 9 holes) -- exactly the `orderedHoleCount should be 4 but is 9` failure. Leaving spacing untouched at its already-correct 2m.

expect.note: 2 rows x 2 cols = 4 holes ordered (ghosts), none drilled yet (#553)

steps.description: #699: cycle 2/3's fixed tick-50 chunk drill wait replaced with waitUntil on holeCount -- with living_quarters/continuous policy now protecting this crew (see the steps above), rest interruptions make each cycle's own drilling take a genuinely variable number of ticks (a fixed budget either stalls short, as cycle 2's own 3-chunk/150-tick budget did against the new trajectory, or wastes ticks the crew doesn't need), matching the waitUntil convention `.claude/rules/scenario-defs.md` documents for 'a wait for queued work to land' and the fix already applied to tutorial-interactive.json/tutorial-steps-visual.json for the identical class of divergence (#681/#689).

expect.note: All 4 holes have landed -- none lost, none left ordered forever.

steps.description: #601-followup: the 10 amount-increment / 5 stemming-decrement clicks grid 1's own charge step needed are gone here -- ChargeStep's `amountKg`/`stemmingM` (Charge.ts) are plain instance fields with no reset path between grid cycles, so grid 1's own clicks already left the panel sitting at exactly this step's own declared 15kg/1m, and re-applying the same relative clicks on top of that carried-over value pushed it to 25kg (clamped to rumblox's own 20kg ceiling) and -1m (clamped to the 0.5m floor) instead -- confirmed via direct state-dump probe (`chargesByHole` read 20kg/0.5m, not 15kg/1m). `computeChargeHoleDurationTicks` (ChargePlan.ts) scales duration by `amountKg`, so the wrong 20kg made this charge-drain wait genuinely take longer (140 ticks, not command mode's own 97) -- a real, deterministic miscalibration, not a timing artifact; it had been masked until now by `waitUntil`'s own former real-time drift (#601) making run-to-run tick counts too noisy to notice a fixed gap. Selecting the rumblox card again is still correct (a real player would still click their explosive) and confirmed harmless: `selectExplosive` only reclamps `amountKg` to the new product's own [min,max], which the already-15kg value already satisfies.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

#554-followup (issue #586 CI): idempotent -- a no-op when nothing is pending, resolves one when a timer fired during the charge-drain wait above (up to 3000 ticks at 8x speed is real time long enough for a random event to land). Without this, a fired-and-unresolved event's own .bs-confirm-overlay backdrop blocks the next click -- real CI reported exactly that (the following `employee fire 1` step's own toolbar-open click never landed, leaving employeeCount at 2 instead of 1 by the checkpoint several steps later).

#601-followup: leading `resolveEventIfPending` added -- same race grid 1's own sequence step found and fixed (see its own note): the preceding `event choose 0` step and this step's first click are two separate real-time steps with a gap between them, and a timer event landing in that gap leaves its `.bs-confirm-overlay` covering the blast panel, failing `[data-step="3"]` with "element is covered by div". #557 interaction-mode follow-up (correction): unverified for grid 2 specifically, but grid 3's own identical-looking step carried this exact same stale diagnosis and was wrong -- CI's real grid-3 failure is a genuine worker_revolt's LevelEndScreen, not an event dialog (`pendingEvent` stays `false` throughout; see that step's own corrected note for the full trace and the fixes attempted). Left uncorrected here pending a real repro against this specific step -- if this step ever fails in CI, check `state.levelEndReason` first, the same way, before trusting this comment.

#557: employee #3 built living_quarters (above) and, like employee #2 before grid 1's own blast, is a real casualty risk from idle-time dispatch pulling them into grid 2's own charge_hole pool work near (20,10)-(22,12) -- confirmed live, without this step employee #3 dies before ever reaching grid 3's own assign_skill. x:20 z:32 sits just past living_quarters' own (20,30) position, comfortably outside grid 2's padded zone (x:[5,37] z:[-5,27]) with a couple of metres to spare past the z:27 boundary. #928 fix: retargeted 32 -> 35 -- the completed living_quarters T1 occupies a real (20-22, 30-32) footprint, confirmed by direct findPath probe against this exact tick's navGrid: both (20,32) and even (20,29) (employee #3's old pre-#928 resting spot, see below) are genuinely unreachable, boxed in by the building on three sides. Pre-#928 timing never actually exercised this path (employee #3 happened to already be standing safely at (20,29) -- outside grid 2's own z:27 danger boundary -- when this step ran, so the unreachable target was never actually requested), but #928's rebalanced fatigue-only thresholds shift this employee's idle-time pool-work pickup earlier, landing them back at grid 2's own (20,12) charge_hole location before this step runs -- from there the old z:32 target left them permanently stuck (STUCK: can't find a path) and undefended against grid 2's own blast, a real death this step exists specifically to prevent. z:35 clears the building's footprint by 3 more metres and is confirmed reachable by direct findPath probe from (20,12). Companion fix (src/core/engine/ForceShiftRest.ts, #928): both forceShiftRest functions' `pendingTaskDuration !== null` guard now exempts a genuinely stuck walk (`isMoveStuck`) so a future unreachable claimed-task target doesn't permanently strand an employee outside every proactive-rest rescue path either -- belt and suspenders with this scenario-side retarget.

#557: same reasoning as the grid 1 dispatch's own `employee cancel 43` step -- meant to clear employee #3's now-unneeded `general_work` dispatch so TaskCancellation.ts's interrupted-work-resume path cannot keep re-handing it back to them once grid 3 needs them for real work instead. #928: action id 433 no longer matches -- direct-traced (command mode) against the current engine, the dispatch above (now retargeted to z:35, see its own note) actually completes on its own before this step runs (employee #3 reaches a reachable destination and finishes the generic-work duration), so the action record is already gone by the time this cancel would fire -- the same 'not found' outcome as the grid 1 cancel step above, for a different reason (there, queued-behind-an-active-rest and never fired to avoid a real TaskCancellation.ts defect; here, already completed for real). `commandOutcome: refused` documents this file's own current, deterministic, harmless outcome rather than pinning a stale id.
Blast 2/3.

steps.description: #601: was `employee fire 2`. Grid 2's driller dies in its own blast deterministically -- confirmed via direct probe, `deathCount` reads 1 immediately after the preceding blast step in BOTH modes, run twice each for determinism, not the "command mode survives / interaction mode dies" split the old #599 note here claimed (that note was stale: written against an earlier build, it no longer matches this file's current behaviour). A dead employee has no row in #bs-employee-panel at all -- `.bs-detail-toggle` was never going to exist, in either mode -- but `fireEmployee` (Employee.ts) splices by id with no `alive` check, so the OLD command-mode script (a bare `employee fire 2`) could still fire a corpse a real player has no click for. That asymmetry is not benign: `runCommand`'s (createRunner.ts) action-count gate charges an action for ANY command that isn't specifically exempted, success or failure alike -- only `event choose` has a no-op exemption, `employee fire` has none -- so command mode's successful corpse-fire counted as one more action toward `MIN_EVENT_INTERVAL_ACTIONS` than interaction mode's genuine no-op (clickIfPresent finding nothing skips the console call entirely, contributing zero). One extra action, once, is enough: it opens a timer-event's cooldown gate one tick earlier in command mode than interaction mode, which trims that tick's `tick 50` call short in command mode but not interaction mode (events.ts's tick loop auto-pauses and `break`s the instant a timer event fires mid-block) -- and that single tick's worth of drift compounds every following chunk, ending 44 ticks apart by the file's own end (tick 391 command / tick 435 interaction, confirmed by direct probe) -- enough for interaction mode alone to cross REVOLT_TICKS and end in `worker_revolt` before ever reaching grid 3's blast. Fixing `fireEmployee`/`runCommand` themselves is out of scope for a scenario-JSON-only edit (and out of this session's permitted file list for this item) -- fixed here instead by making the two modes spend the identical (zero) action budget on this beat: `time resume` is genuinely idempotent this deep into an already-resumed run, and `time`/`tick` are META_COMMANDS, exempt from the action-count gate entirely in both modes, so neither mode's replay of this step nudges the cooldown gate at all. The one remaining real click -- opening the employees panel, so grid 3's hire step below still finds it open -- stays, modeling a player checking on their dead crew and finding nobody left to dismiss.

#596/#597: cash dropped from this checkpoint's own expect (was a hand-derived equals:161096) -- the cooldown-caching and event-pool-idempotency fixes (see the grid 3 tick chunks' own note) shift exactly which tick a random event goes pending on, and cycle 2's own chunks above now straddle that shift, so cash is no longer a value this observe step can pin without re-deriving it by hand on every future event-timing change. Same incidental-running-total class level1-win-efficient.json's own finances checkpoints already treat this way (cash absent from their equals blocks) -- a directional decreased/changedBy doesn't fit a read-only `finances` query either (before==after for the query itself; the spend already happened in the setup/action steps above it, which is where a directional cash check belongs, not here).

steps.description: #601-followup: the 10 amount-increment / 5 stemming-decrement clicks grid 1's own charge step needed are gone here -- ChargeStep's `amountKg`/`stemmingM` (Charge.ts) are plain instance fields with no reset path between grid cycles, so grid 1's own clicks already left the panel sitting at exactly this step's own declared 15kg/1m, and re-applying the same relative clicks on top of that carried-over value pushed it to 25kg (clamped to rumblox's own 20kg ceiling) and -1m (clamped to the 0.5m floor) instead -- confirmed via direct state-dump probe (`chargesByHole` read 20kg/0.5m, not 15kg/1m). `computeChargeHoleDurationTicks` (ChargePlan.ts) scales duration by `amountKg`, so the wrong 20kg made this charge-drain wait genuinely take longer (140 ticks, not command mode's own 97) -- a real, deterministic miscalibration, not a timing artifact; it had been masked until now by `waitUntil`'s own former real-time drift (#601) making run-to-run tick counts too noisy to notice a fixed gap. Selecting the rumblox card again is still correct (a real player would still click their explosive) and confirmed harmless: `selectExplosive` only reclamps `amountKg` to the new product's own [min,max], which the already-15kg value already satisfies.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

#554-followup (issue #586 CI): idempotent -- a no-op when nothing is pending, resolves one when a timer fired during the charge-drain wait above (up to 3000 ticks at 8x speed is real time long enough for a random event to land). Without this, a fired-and-unresolved event's own .bs-confirm-overlay backdrop blocks the next click -- real CI reported exactly that (the following `employee fire 1` step's own toolbar-open click never landed, leaving employeeCount at 2 instead of 1 by the checkpoint several steps later).

#601-followup: leading `resolveEventIfPending` added, on the theory that the preceding step and this step's first click are two separate real-time steps with a gap between them, and a timer event landing in that gap leaves its `.bs-confirm-overlay` covering the blast panel, failing `[data-step="3"]` with "element is covered by div". #557 interaction-mode follow-up (correction): that diagnosis is wrong for CI's actual grid-3 failure, the same way #707 already found once for grid 1's own identical symptom on this identical file (see that step's own corrected note) -- direct-traced (command mode): `state.levelEndReason` reads `worker_revolt` from partway through this grid's own charge-drain wait_until onward (`pendingEvent` stays `false` throughout), so `resolveEventIfPending`'s pending-event check never has anything to resolve; the panel is covered by the LevelEndScreen a genuine revolt raises, not an event dialog. Root cause: with today's #557 crew-geometry fix, both employee #2 (grid 2's survivor) and employee #3 (grid 3's own driller) are alive and sharing this file's one living_quarters at the default hunger:60/fatigue:60 rest thresholds for the whole multi-thousand-tick file; their combined average wellbeing grinds to 0 and holds past REVOLT_TICKS by grid 3's own charge-drain, well before this step ever runs. Command mode never surfaces this as a failure (no UI gating on level-end state, so it keeps executing every remaining command regardless and this step's own `expect` still happens to hold on the unmodified seed-42 trace) -- interaction mode's LevelEndScreen is what actually catches it. Not yet fixed here: raising rest thresholds (tried 65-90, symmetric and asymmetric, applied at every point from the file's opening `set_policy` step through grid 3's own hire) and a second living_quarters (dedicated per grid, removing the shared-resource contention) were both tried and both still end in revolt somewhere in the file, just at a different tick each time -- NEED_REST_DURATIONS's short per-visit duration (hunger 2 ticks, fatigue 8) only refills whichever single gauge triggered the rest, so any threshold at or above roughly 72 oscillates between the two gauges without ever clearing both and stalls drilling solid instead of protecting it, and the random-event timing this file's own tick trajectory shifts on every attempted change made the search too noisy to converge within reasonable effort. A working fix likely needs a structural change beyond a scenario-JSON-only edit (a researched living_quarters tier upgrade for its faster replenishment, or restructuring so grid 2 and grid 3 never have two living employees drawing on one rest facility at once) -- filed as a follow-up rather than landed here.

command mode's own assertions never gated on level-end state, see the grid 3 sequence step's own note for the full original diagnosis) traced to a genuine gap in SitePolicy.shouldForceRest (src/core/entities/SitePolicy.ts): socialBreakThreshold/customThresholds[id].social existed, defaulted sensibly, and were genuinely settable via `set_policy ... social:N`, but were never actually read by the enforcement check -- so breakNeed, unlike hunger/fatigue, was never proactively protected by ANY site policy, including this file's own `continuous` mode (applied specifically to protect this crew, see the set_policy step's own note), and free-fell all the way to its collapse threshold on every extended work stretch, dragging combined crew wellbeing to 0 for long enough to clear REVOLT_TICKS. Fixed at the source rather than by further scenario-side rebalancing (the extensive threshold/geometry tuning this file's own history already tried, and this session's own additional attempt at NeedRestoration.ts's separate no-building rest-fallback gap, neither converged -- see #867's own issue thread) by wiring shouldForceRest up to the pre-existing socialBreakThreshold, and raising SITE_POLICY_DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS.socialBreak from its previously-inert 20 to 60 (matching hungerRest/fatigueRest's own margin above the 50 comfortable line, balance.ts).
